text:
FAILOVER: Ads Agent did not report within the 360-second answer guarantee (a read-only recovery ping was already sent; no work was re-dispatched to it). PLL Consultant pulled this directly from live Google Ads and Outlook data.

SCOPE: The two net-new Ads-Agent campaigns only — PLL-Search-ContractMfg-2026 (24049588003) and PLL-Search-Samples-2026 (24040031889), covering all 7 in-scope ad groups. Legacy campaigns (Initial, New-Sales-Ad, Sales Campaign PLL) are excluded entirely from every figure below.

TODAY (2026-08-05, partial day as of ~7pm ET pull): Combined 10 clicks, 52 impressions, $23.89 spend, 19.2% CTR, $2.39 avg CPC. ContractMfg: 9 clicks, 40 impr, $22.39, 22.5% CTR, $2.49 CPC (budget $20.33/day). Samples: 1 click, 12 impr, $1.50, 8.3% CTR, $1.50 CPC (budget $5.00/day).

TRAILING 7 DAYS (Jul 30–Aug 5) vs PRIOR 7 DAYS (Jul 23–Jul 29): Combined 78 clicks vs 73 (+6.8%), 553 impr vs 431 (+28.3%), $212.26 spend vs $134.17 (+58.2%), 14.1% CTR vs 16.9%, $2.72 avg CPC vs $1.84 (+47.8%). ContractMfg: 42 clicks/$158.97/12.5% CTR/$3.78 CPC vs 39 clicks/$83.58/19.1% CTR/$2.14 CPC — spend nearly doubled (+90%) for only +7.7% more clicks, CPC up 76.6%. Samples: 36 clicks/$53.29/16.7% CTR/$1.48 CPC vs 34 clicks/$50.59/15.0% CTR/$1.49 CPC — essentially flat.

AD-GROUP BREAKDOWN (trailing 7d, all 7 in-scope ad groups): Samples-PrivateLabel-Products $53.29 (36 clicks, 16.7% CTR, $1.48 CPC) — solid, largest volume. ContractMfg-Skincare $20.92 (9 clicks, 20.0% CTR, $2.32 CPC) — best efficiency at meaningful volume. ProductIntent-BeefTallow $2.17 (2 clicks, 28.6% CTR, $1.08 CPC) — efficient, tiny volume. ContractMfg-Haircare $24.08 (8 clicks, 11.0% CTR, $3.01 CPC) — mid-pack. ProductIntent-HairOil $7.40 (1 click, 33.3% CTR, $7.40 CPC) — N too small to judge. ContractMfg-Cosmetic-Beauty $104.39 (22 clicks, 10.5% CTR, $4.75 CPC) — WORST: ~49% of the week's combined spend at the weakest CTR and highest CPC among active groups; top reallocation candidate. ProductIntent-BeardOil $0.00 (0 impressions) — DORMANT, needs a bid/keyword/targeting fix or an explicit pause decision.

SEARCH TERMS / WASTE: Search-term-level reporting is not obtainable with the currently approved Google Ads tools (no search_term_view resource in scope) — cannot quantify a wasted-spend dollar figure this run. This is a known, previously flagged tool gap, not a new problem. The clearest evidence-backed inefficiency signal available this run is the Cosmetic-Beauty ad group above.

LEADS — INBOX (Outlook sam@prvtlabellabs.com): Qualified inbound inquiries (Shopify "New customer message" contact-form submissions): 7 in the trailing 7d vs 16 raw / ~15 unique in the prior 7d (one apparent duplicate double-submission on 7/27) — down roughly 56%. Google-Ads-attributed (gclid/gbraid present in the lead-source field): 3 of 7 in trailing 7d (all unique) vs 3 raw / 2 unique in prior 7d — held roughly steady, did NOT decline with the rest of the inbox. ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: a gclid proves the click came from SOME Google Ads campaign; it does not prove which one. Legacy Google Ads campaigns are also live in this account, so these gclid leads are NOT YET MEASURABLE as specifically belonging to the two net-new scoped campaigns versus legacy ones. Sample size is very small (3 vs 3/2) — not enough alone to call a hard trend. Approx CPL using combined net-new ad spend over gclid-carrying leads (same caveat applies): ~$70.75 trailing7d vs ~$67–$70 prior7d — both under the $75 two-week escalation threshold but close to it. Booked calls: 2 discovery-call meeting records found in the trailing 7d window (Rehman Ghani 8/3, Alexander Peterkin 7/30) — not confirmed ad-attributed. Google Ads itself shows 0 conversions in every window for both campaigns — expected, since there is no conversion tag and PLL counts leads manually from the inbox per standing policy.

FUNNEL HEALTH — PRIME SUSPECT: Paid clicks were healthy and rose (+6.8%) while TOTAL qualified inbox inquiries fell by more than half. Ads-specific (gclid) submissions held steady. That pattern — healthy clicks, collapsing total emails — matches exactly the known open defect: the website homepage quote form reportedly drops submissions and Contact Us routes away from Sam. Rank this the #1 suspect and verify/live-test it today.

BUDGET CAP: Currently configured $20.33/day (ContractMfg) + $5.00/day (Samples) = $25.33/day (~$177.31/wk). Actual trailing-7d combined spend was $212.26 (~119.7% of that weekly figure). NOT declaring a confirmed cap breach: Samples' daily budget appears to have changed mid-window (consistent with a previously flagged, unexplained drop from ~$10.33/day to $5.00/day around 8/3–8/4), so comparing the full 7-day spend against today's configured rate alone is not valid. This needs re-verification of the actual budget-per-day history; flagging for Sam, not claiming an overspend.

RECOMMENDATION (one action): Before changing anything in Google Ads, have someone submit a real test lead through the homepage quote form and the Contact Us page today and confirm it lands in Sam's inbox. This is the single highest-leverage check because it explains the "not enough emails" feeling far better than ad performance does — clicks are healthy, the inbox isn't. If the form is confirmed healthy, the next Ads-side move (pending Sam's approval, no budget change) would be reallocating spend away from the underperforming Cosmetic-Beauty ad group toward Skincare/Samples/BeefTallow, and deciding whether to fix or pause the dormant BeardOil ad group.
spoken_text: Ads Agent didn't report back, so I pulled this myself. Here's the bottom line: over the last seven days our two new campaigns got a few more clicks and a lot more impressions than the week before, but cost per click jumped almost fifty percent, so we spent nearly sixty percent more for barely more traffic. Total emails landing in the inbox fell by more than half compared to the week before, but the handful we can actually trace to a Google ad click held steady, and I can't yet confirm those specific clicks came from our two new campaigns versus your older ones. My read is this isn't really an ads problem: clicks were healthy while total inbound emails collapsed, and that points straight at the broken homepage quote form and Contact Us routing you already know about. I recommend testing that form today, before we touch anything in Google Ads.
